concepts.title: Constructions with Ruler and Compass
concepts.definition: Geometric figures are drawn precisely with instruments: a ruler draws and measures line segments, and a compass copies lengths and cuts arcs, so that a segment of an exact given length can be constructed anywhere.
concepts.key_idea: Construction is drawing with proof: compass arcs guarantee that the copied length is exactly the given one.

concepts.title: Squares and Rectangles by Construction
concepts.definition: Squares and rectangles are constructed from their properties: a rectangle needs opposite sides equal and four right angles, a square needs four equal sides and four right angles, so each side and corner is checked with compass and set square while building.
concepts.key_idea: Properties are the instruction manual: equal sides and right angles, applied step by step, build exact figures.

concepts.title: Right Angles in Constructions
concepts.definition: Right angles anchor most constructions: folding paper, using a set square or drawing arcs from two points on a segment gives perpendicular lines, and the corners of squares and rectangles are verified as exact right angles.
concepts.key_idea: A right angle is the square's signature: without four of them, the figure collapses into an ordinary quadrilateral.

concepts.title: Figures Made of Line Segments
concepts.definition: Complex figures are walks of line segments joined endpoint to endpoint; counting the segments, copying their lengths one by one and joining carefully reproduces any stick-figure design exactly.
concepts.key_idea: Every drawing is a chain of segments: lengths and joints, measured and matched, rebuild the whole figure.
